seed: ONE KIND OF LABEL, ONE SIZE. Reading every label of a screenshot back into words already settles the typeface for the whole picture and the weight for each kind of label. The size was still decided label by label: six row labels that are 13 points on screen came back 27.6, 28.0, 28.5, 28.0, 28.5 and 28.4 points, so picking all six showed Size reading Mixed and anybody who then set a size was tidying up after the app. The walk reads a settings pane, picks its six row labels together and asks the panel what size they are; then it does the same to this app's own Effects panel, where the section labels really are bigger than the rows under them and each group has to settle on one size without dragging the other onto it.

steps.note: Every label in the pane is real text now. The six rows of the two cards are the thing to look at: they are one size in the picture, and until this landed each of them came back at whatever size its own ink measured, a third of a point apart.

THE FIRST TEST, and the whole point of the task: all six row labels picked at once, and the Size menu says one number. It used to say Mixed, which is the app telling you in one word that six labels which are identical on screen came back six different sizes.

THE SECOND TEST: settling the size must not flatten the page. The heading over those rows is half again their size, so it is not a label of their kind and it comes back at its own size, exactly as it did before.

This app's own Effects panel. The section labels Corner Radius, Border 1 and Border 2 are a shade bigger than the Style, Color, Position, Width and Offset rows under them, and both groups used to wobble by a third of a point inside themselves.
THE THIRD TEST: the three section labels picked together read one size instead of Mixed.

THE FOURTH TEST, and the one that says this settles wobble rather than flattening a page: the five rows under those sections read one size too, and it is a SMALLER one. The panel comes back reading like the panel.
